text: Which of these nouns keeps the same spelling in the plural?
gloss: Which of these nouns keeps the same spelling in the plural? — Deer: the others become geese, mice and teeth.

text: Which of these words is a noun or a verb depending on which syllable you stress?
gloss: Which word is a noun or a verb depending on the stressed syllable? — Record: a REcord, to reCORD.

text: Which of these words sounds exactly like “flower”?
gloss: Which word sounds exactly like 'flower'? — Flour: a homophone; floor, flavour and flare sound different.

text: Someone who says they are “under the weather” is feeling what?
gloss: Someone who is 'under the weather' is feeling what? — Unwell: the idiom means slightly ill.

text: A packet of “crisps” in Britain is a bag of what in the United States?
gloss: A packet of 'crisps' in Britain is a bag of what in the US? — Chips: Americans say 'chips' for crisps and 'fries' for British chips.

text: What is a traditional British “ploughman’s lunch” mainly made of?
gloss: What is a ploughman's lunch mainly? — Bread, cheese and pickle, a cold pub plate.

text: On an American form, which date does “04/07” stand for?
gloss: On an American form, which date is 04/07? — 7 April: Americans write the month first; in Britain it would be 4 July.

text: In Australia, in which season does Christmas fall?
gloss: In Australia, in which season does Christmas fall? — Summer: the seasons are reversed south of the equator.

text: Which US state is made up of islands in the middle of the Pacific?
gloss: Which US state is made up of islands in the mid-Pacific? — Hawaii: an island chain, the 50th state.

text: Which of these birds is named after the sound it makes?
gloss: Which bird is named after its call? — Cuckoo: the name imitates its two-note cry.

text: In cricket, what do we call a batter who is out without scoring a run?
gloss: In cricket, what is a batter out for zero called? — A duck: from 'duck's egg', the shape of a zero.

text: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football?
gloss: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football? — 6: the kick afterwards adds one more.

text: Which tree’s winged seeds spin down to the ground like little helicopters?
gloss: Which tree's winged seeds spin down like helicopters? — The maple (the sycamore is one); oak has acorns, birch tiny flakes, willow fluff.

text: Which UK nation has a red dragon on its flag?
gloss: Which UK nation has a red dragon on its flag? — Wales: Y Ddraig Goch.

text: Which British monarch celebrated a Platinum Jubilee in 2022?
gloss: Which British monarch celebrated a Platinum Jubilee in 2022? — Elizabeth II, after 70 years on the throne.

text: Which reed did the ancient Egyptians use to make an early kind of paper?
gloss: Which reed did ancient Egyptians make paper from? — Papyrus, which also gave English the word 'paper'.

text: Which animal is the national emblem of Canada?
gloss: Which animal is Canada's national emblem? — The beaver, made official in 1975.

text: Which bestselling series follows the archer Katniss Everdeen?
gloss: Which bestselling series follows Katniss Everdeen? — The Hunger Games.

text: Which mythical bird is said to burst into flames and rise again from its ashes?
gloss: Which mythical bird bursts into flames and rises from its ashes? — The phoenix.

text: In which video game do hissing creepers sneak up and explode?
gloss: In which video game do hissing creepers explode? — Minecraft.

text: Which TV baking contest takes place in a large white tent in the English countryside?
gloss: Which baking contest is held in a white tent in the countryside? — The Great British Bake Off.

text: On a standard English keyboard, which letter sits between T and U?
gloss: On a QWERTY keyboard, which letter sits between T and U? — Y (Q W E R T Y U I O P).

text: Which song do people traditionally sing at midnight on New Year’s Eve?
gloss: Which song is sung at midnight on New Year's Eve? — Auld Lang Syne, Robert Burns's words.

text: Which number do Americans dial in an emergency?
gloss: Which number do Americans dial in an emergency? — 911; 999 is the British number and 000 the Australian one.

text: Which of these instruments belongs to the brass family?
gloss: Which instrument belongs to the brass family? — Trumpet; the flute is metal but counts as woodwind.

text: Which vitamin does the skin make when it is in sunlight?
gloss: Which vitamin does skin make in sunlight? — Vitamin D.

text: What makes a compass needle point north?
gloss: What makes a compass needle point north? — Earth's magnetic field.

text: Which anonymous street artist from Bristol is known for stencils like “Girl with Balloon”?
gloss: Which anonymous Bristol street artist made 'Girl with Balloon'? — Banksy.

text: Which month’s name comes from the Latin word for “eight”?
gloss: Which month's name comes from Latin for 'eight'? — October (octo); it was the 8th month in the old Roman calendar.

text: Which US coin is worth more than a nickel but is physically smaller?
gloss: Which US coin is worth more than a nickel yet smaller? — The dime (10 cents), smaller than the nickel (5 cents).

text: Which metal in the skin of the Statue of Liberty gave it its green colour?
gloss: Which metal in the Statue of Liberty's skin turned it green? — Copper, which develops a green patina.

text: Which bird stands beside the kangaroo on Australia’s coat of arms?
gloss: Which bird stands beside the kangaroo on Australia's coat of arms? — The emu.

text: A golfer who finishes a hole one stroke under par has made a what?
gloss: One stroke under par is a what? — A birdie; an eagle is two under, a bogey one over.

text: On which day of the week is American Thanksgiving always held?
gloss: Which weekday is US Thanksgiving always on? — Thursday, the fourth Thursday of November.

text: Which Marvel superhero is billionaire inventor Tony Stark?
gloss: Which Marvel hero is Tony Stark? — Iron Man; Batman is DC's billionaire, Bruce Wayne.

text: On which ship did Charles Darwin sail round the world in the 1830s?
gloss: On which ship did Darwin sail in the 1830s? — HMS Beagle (1831-36); Endeavour was Cook's, Bounty is the mutiny.

text: Which company created the Windows operating system?
gloss: Which company created Windows? — Microsoft.

text: In British legend, what is the name of King Arthur’s sword?
gloss: What is King Arthur's sword called? — Excalibur; Durandal is Roland's, Gram Sigurd's, Joyeuse Charlemagne's.

text: Which Canadian dish is made of fries topped with cheese curds and gravy?
gloss: Which Canadian dish is fries with cheese curds and gravy? — Poutine, from Quebec.

text: In music, what does the Italian word “forte” tell the performer to do?
gloss: What does 'forte' tell a performer to do? — Play loudly (piano means softly).

text: Which Roman wall runs across northern England, from coast to coast?
gloss: Which Roman wall crosses northern England coast to coast? — Hadrian's Wall (AD 122); the Antonine Wall is in Scotland, Offa's Dyke is Anglo-Saxon, Watling Street a road.

text: Which canal joins the Atlantic and Pacific oceans across Central America?
gloss: Which canal joins the Atlantic and Pacific across Central America? — The Panama Canal (1914).

text: Which of these words does not rhyme with the other three?
gloss: Which word does not rhyme with the others? — Cough (rhymes with 'off'); tough, rough, enough end in '-uff'.

text: Which Scottish scientist discovered penicillin in 1928?
gloss: Which Scottish scientist discovered penicillin in 1928? — Alexander Fleming.

text: Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic?
gloss: Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic? — Amelia Earhart, in 1932.

text: Which poet wrote “I wandered lonely as a cloud”?
gloss: Who wrote 'I wandered lonely as a cloud'? — William Wordsworth, the daffodils poem.

text: Which architect designed Barcelona’s unfinished Sagrada Família?
gloss: Which architect designed the Sagrada Família? — Antoni Gaudí.

text: The equator crosses all of these countries except which one?
gloss: The equator crosses all but which? — Peru; it crosses Brazil, Ecuador and Kenya.

text: Which Dutch artist painted “The Milkmaid” and “View of Delft”?
gloss: Which Dutch artist painted 'The Milkmaid' and 'View of Delft'? — Johannes Vermeer.

text: Which element was detected in the Sun’s light before it was found on Earth?
gloss: Which element was seen in sunlight before being found on Earth? — Helium (1868 in the solar spectrum; on Earth 1895).
